issue: BLOCKING. rails-env reads raw_config.env.dig('clear','RAILS_ENV') instead of Kamal's resolved env, contradicting its own docstring (L25-26, 'rather than re-implementing') and the CHANGELOG claim that credentials are never encrypted for an environment the app will not run. A role-level override (servers.web.env.clear.RAILS_ENV: staging over base production) prints 'production' while Kamal's primary_role.env(host).clear gives 'staging' = wrong credentials env. The flat form env: {RAILS_ENV: production}, which Kamal accepts (configuration/env.rb L8), exits 2 and says RAILS_ENV is unset. Disposition: fixed: rails-env asks Kamal for Role#env(host).clear on every role and host; exits 2 when none set it or they disagree (set beside unset counts). Real-loader fixtures for the role override, the flat form and disagreeing roles, mocked fixtures for each branch, and mutations restoring the dig, reading the raw clear hash per role, and accepting disagreement.
repro: scratchpad/role and scratchpad/flat configs: python3 kamal_destination.py rails-env -> production / UNUSABLE; ruby Kamal loader -> staging / {RAILS_ENV=>production}

issue: Suggestion. 'RAILS_MASTER_KEY is the key of the credentials file rails-env names' is ambiguous, because rails-env prints two keys: key (the one read today) and write_key (the new pair). On a fresh app they differ (config/master.key and config/credentials/production.key), yet the snippet writes to write_content. kamal-configurator.md has the same sentence. Disposition: fixed: both prose files say RAILS_MASTER_KEY is the contents of rails-env's write_key, not its key.
fix_options: Name write_key explicitly, or say to re-run rails-env after the write and use its key

issue: Suggestion (pre-existing, now more reachable). The snippet always creates config/credentials/<env>.yml.enc. When the app has only config/credentials.yml.enc, Rails then stops reading the shared file (railties configuration.rb L643-650, per the PR's own citation), so existing keys such as secret_key_base disappear unless they are carried over. The new 'content' field rails-env prints is never used. Disposition: fixed: the configurator snippet seeds a new per-environment file from rails-env's content/key (CREDENTIALS_CONTENT/CREDENTIALS_KEY) and dropped the rescue that swallowed a wrong key; deploy-cloud.md states the shadowing.
fix_options: Seed the new per-env file from the 'content' file before merging
Or write into the content/key pair when no per-env file exists

issue: Suggestion [Recall, not verified this session]. The doctrine routes a non-production RAILS_ENV to the overlay without saying that the app then needs config/environments/<env>.rb and a database.yml entry for that env. Without the database.yml entry, boot fails at db:prepare. Disposition: fixed after doctrine-verifier CONFIRMED against railties/activerecord 8.1.4 (engine.rb L564-568; database_configurations.rb L214-216, L304-308): both prose files name config/environments/<env>.rb and a database.yml entry, and STOP when either is missing.
fix_options: Add one line naming these prerequisites, verified via doctrine-verifier
